Plot a fitted model

Source: R/plot.R
plot.bef_fit_re.Rd

The plot() method for a fitted model shows the plot selected by type. Each type is produced by one of the package's plot functions, e.g., "sites" by plot_sites() and "g" by plot_g(), and further arguments are passed on to that function. See Details for all types.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit_re'
plot(x, type = "sites", ..., backend = NULL)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

type

The plot to show, e.g., "sites" (the default), "g" or "shrinkage". See Details for all types.

...

Further arguments passed to the plot function for type, such as level, sort_by or scale.

backend

Deprecated. backend = "base" plots the types "caterpillar", "g", "diagnostic" and "loo" with base graphics instead of ggplot2 and issues a warning. This option will be removed.

Value

A ggplot object, which can be modified with ggplot2 functions, e.g., by adding layers. For type = "mcmc", the value returned by plot_mcmc(). With backend = "base", the plot is shown on the current graphics device and NULL is returned invisibly.

Details

type can be one of the following. The help page of each function describes the plot and its arguments.

  • "sites" (the default): plot_sites(), a caterpillar plot of the site effects with their posterior intervals

  • "g": plot_g(), the estimated distribution of effects

  • "shrinkage": plot_shrinkage(), a shrinkage plot of posterior means against estimates

  • "exceedance": plot_exceedance(), the probability that each effect exceeds a threshold

  • "site_posterior": plot_site_posterior(), the posterior distribution of the effect of each site specified in sites

  • "diagnostics": plot_diagnostics(), sampler and grid diagnostics

  • "loo": plot_loo(), the Pareto k values of the sites from leave-one-out cross-validation

  • "ppc": plot_ppc(), a posterior predictive check of the model against the estimates

  • "mcmc": plot_mcmc(), trace plots and other plots of the posterior draws

  • "grid": plot.bef_grid(), the grid in relation to the estimates

  • "recovery": plot_recovery(), a comparison of the fit with the known true effects specified in truth

"caterpillar" and "diagnostic" are accepted as aliases for "sites" and "diagnostics".

type = "g" shows the density of \(g\). To plot the probabilities of the grid points instead, call plot_g(x, type = "mass"). Note that their heights depend on the number of grid points.

See also

plot_sites(), plot_g(), bef_fit, diagnose(), vignette("plots")

Examples

plot(krw_fit, n_extreme = 10, scale = 100)

plot(krw_fit, type = "g", scale = 100)

plot(krw_fit, type = "diagnostics")


# The result is a ggplot object, so labels and layers can be added.
plot(krw_fit, type = "shrinkage", scale = 100) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Estimated gap (percentage points)")
